author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary
This page consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical guidance for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, packaging and installation guidance, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback workflows, and a customer requirements library used by Solutions and Sales to validate proposals. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, solutions engineers, and authorized customer engineering teams.

1) Scope and goals
- Provide reproducible, secure, and auditable deployment patterns for VPC-hosted and on-prem installations.
- Minimize downtime and operational risk during upgrades.
- Standardize day-2 ops (monitoring, backups, scaling) and handover requirements for customers.

2) Supported topologies (high level)
- VPC Single-Region (recommended for most customers): control plane in customer VPC, data plane in private subnets, optional NAT/egress through customer-managed NAT gateway.
- VPC Multi-Region: active region + warm standby region for DR; routed via customer managed load balancers.
- On-Prem Isolated Cluster: air-gapped option for regulated customers; supports GPU nodes and on-site KMS/HSM integration.

3) Reference architectures (summaries)
A. VPC production (3-tier logical):
- Tier 1: Control Plane (API, auth, web console) — private subnets, reachable via bastion or customer VPN.
- Tier 2: Inference Fleet (GPU nodes) — private subnets with SGs allowing internal cluster traffic and egress for telemetry only.
- Tier 3: Storage & Caching (S3-compatible object store, Redis or Memcached) — access limited to cluster subnets.

B. VPC with DMZ and dedicated egress:..
- DMZ load balancers terminate TLS and forward to control plane in private subnets.
- Egress via NAT instances/boxes that provide centralized outbound filtering and egress logging.

C. On-Prem air-gapped cluster:
- Kubernetes or bare-metal cluster inside customer network.
- Optional hardware HSM/KMS for key isolation.
- Image registry mirror and update appliance for controlled patching.

4) Pre-deployment checklist (customer & Redwood)
Customer prerequisites (to be validated by Solutions Engineer):
1. VPC network CIDR blocks, public/private subnet allocation, and available IPs.
2. Firewall rules and security group templates.
3. IAM/KMS access model (customer KMS ARN for encrypted secrets).
4. Required DNS records and TLS certificate issuance process.
5. Storage endpoints (S3 or S3-compatible) and retention requirements.
6. GPU instance types and count (for on-prem, GPU model and driver compatibility).

Redwood prerequisites:
- Deployment artifact version (Docker image tag / on-prem package hash).
- Deployment runbook assigned and owners listed.
- Test plan for smoke tests and canary verification.

5) Packaging & installation
Artifacts and packaging options:
- Hosted container images: quay.redwood-inference.com/redwood/api:VERSION, /runtime:VERSION, /scheduler:VERSION.
- On-prem package: tarball containing images, Helm charts, offline registry tar, and an installer binary for air-gapped installs.
- Debian/RPM packages are provided for customers with strict OS management policies.

System requirements (minimum per cluster):
| Component        | Minimum (small) | Recommended (prod) | Notes |
|------------------|-----------------|--------------------|-------|
| Control plane CPU| 4 vCPU          | 8 vCPU             | 2+ replicas for HA |
| Memory (control) | 16 GB           | 32 GB              | JVM heap tuned per config |
| GPU nodes        | 1 x A10         | 4 x A100 (p4d)     | driver and CUDA required |
| Disk (root)      | 100 GB SSD      | 500 GB NVMe        | logs and local caches |
| Object storage   | S3 compat       | S3 with lifecycle  | 2x replication preferred |

Networking and ports (minimal):
- 443/tcp: TLS for control plane endpoints.
- 8443/tcp: internal admin API (restricted to cluster CIDR).
- 2379/tcp: etcd (cluster-internal).
- 6379/tcp: Redis (if used).
- 22/tcp: Bastion access only; no direct node SSH by default.

Installer modes (steps):
- Online (Helm + public registry): "helm repo add redwood https://helm.redwood-inference.com && helm upgrade --install redwood redwood/redwood --namespace redwood --set image.tag=VERSION"
- Air-gapped: Load offline registry image tar into local mirror, install Helm chart with --set image.registry=local.registry:5000 and apply certs from customer PKI.

6) Day-1 (initial verification)
Smoke test checklist (run after install):
1. All pods/services are Running and Ready.
2. Control plane health endpoint returns 200: /_health (auth bypass token for smoke).
3. Sample inference request against local test model returns expected inference token count and latency < configured SLO.
4. Logs present in logging backend; metrics scraped by Prometheus.

7) Day-2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling)
Monitoring & observability:
- Metrics: token/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, queue length.
- Dashboards: per-cluster and per-model dashboards in Redwood Console.
- Alerts (examples):
  - token/sec drops by >40% sustained 5m -> platform degraded (pager).
  - p99 latency > 2x SLO for 5m -> oncall (pager).
  - GPU memory OOM events -> paged to infra team.

Backups & data protection:
- Metadata backups: etcd snapshot every 6 hours; retained 30 days.
- Model artifacts: periodic sync to customer S3; daily incremental.
- KV cache: ephemeral, not backed up; caches restored from warm-start model state.

Scaling and capacity changes:
- Recommended horizontal scaling for inference workers. GPU driver upgrades require maintenance window.
- Autoscaling policy: scale when queue length > X and GPU utilization < 80% triggers scale-out.
- Capacity planning: SRE team conducts quarterly load tests using benchmarking suite in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.

Operational runbook links (must be present in the deployment):
- /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-deployment-runbook-2028-03-01
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-and-error-budgets

8) Upgrade and rollback procedures
Principles:
- Always test upgrades in a staging environment that mirrors prod topology.
- Use canary rollouts with traffic shadowing and progressive promotion.
- Maintain automatic rollback triggers for failed smoke tests or SLO regressions.

Upgrade plan (summary):
1. Prepare release notes and binary/image artifacts. Verify hashes and sign packages.
2. Run migration dry-run in staging; validate data migrations (schema changes).
3. Canary: deploy new control plane image to 1 replica in canary namespace; run smoke tests and load tests for 30-60 minutes.
4. If canary passes, incrementally upgrade control plane replicas (rolling update, maxUnavailable=1).
5. Upgrade inference fleet in waves (node pool by node pool), draining traffic and running post-upgrade inference tests.
6. Post-upgrade verification: full traffic, end-to-end smoke tests, and monitoring for 2x the averaging window for SLOs.

Rollback triggers and steps:
- Automatic triggers: failing smoke test, SLO regression > 10% on p95/p99, crashlooping pods > 3 per minute.
- Manual triggers: operator judgement after investigating alerts.

Rollback procedure (control plane):
1. Pause incoming traffic (route to fallback region or existing stable variant).
2. Re-deploy previous image tag: helm upgrade --install redwood redwood/redwood --set image.tag=PREVIOUS_TAG --namespace redwood --wait --timeout 10m
3. Re-run smoke tests.
4. If etcd or DB schema migration occurred as part of upgrade, consult the migration plan. Some migrations are irreversible — in these cases rollback may require restoring DB snapshot and a restore verification window.

Rollback procedure (inference fleet):
- Drain nodes: kubectl cordon/evict then deploy previous image on drained node pool. Confirm model cache warmup and run sample inferences.

9) Post-incident and post-upgrade validation
- Postmortem: create incident review within 72 hours if any outage > 5 minutes occurs. Include root cause, timeline, impact, remediation, and action owners.
- Quality validation: run regression test suite against production prompt sets (link to /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage).

10) Customer requirements library (select entries)
This section is a condensed extract from the full requirements library used by Solutions when authoring statements of work. Items below should be validated per-customer and documented in the customer runbook.

Network & Security (must provide):
- Dedicated VPC with private subnets for compute.
- Security groups that allow internal service ports only; no public access to control plane APIs.
- KMS access policy with least privilege for Redwood service principal.
- TLS certificates: customer-provided wildcard or SAN cert covering API endpoints.

Compliance & Data residency:
- Data residency: region-specific storage endpoints; object lifecycle and retention configured per contract.
- Audit logging: audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM via TLS; retention 365 days by default (or as contracted).

Operational roles and responsibilities (example mapping):
- Customer: Physical host management, network ACLs, perimeter firewall, on-prem hardware lifecycle.
- Redwood: Software install, runtime configuration, application-level monitoring and SRE escalation.
- Shared: Backup/restore success validation, ransomware protection configuration.

11) Troubleshooting checklist (common failure modes)
- Pod CrashLoopBackOff: check container logs, OOM events, and recent config changes; escalate to runtime team if due to kernel or driver OOM.
- High inference latency: check GPU utilization, queue length, and caching hit rates. Consider warm model cache or scale-out.
- Failure after upgrade: check image tag rollback, DB migration state, and etcd status. Restore etcd snapshot if necessary.

12) Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team (oncall roster in internal PagerDuty group REDWOOD-PD-PRIVATE).
- Release owner: Release Engineering (releases@redwood-inference.com).
- Escalation path: SRE oncall -> Runtime oncall -> Eng leadership.

13) Appendix: example verification commands
- Helm smoke: helm test redwood --namespace redwood
- Health check: curl -k -H "Authorization: Bearer SMOKE_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/_health
- Canary traffic: kubectl apply -f canary-routing.yaml

14) Appendix: model rollout and compatibility notes
- When switching model quantization profiles, validate sample outputs against golden prompts to detect quality regressions.
- Quantized model binary formats must be signed and versioned; store versions in metadata catalog.
